segments.text: This is SeatCraft — an event seating planner built for the WebMCP Challenge. The idea: seating charts are a two-player game. The host knows the social landmines. The agent has the patience for the constraint puzzle. WebMCP lets them share one live board.

Here's a wedding: twenty-four guests, five tables. The host has locked the couple at the head table — those seats are non-negotiable. And there are rules: Aunt Carol and Uncle Jim divorced in 2019, so they can't share a table. Two couples must sit together. Abuela Rosa belongs with family.

The page registers fifteen tools on navigator dot model context — the WebMCP API. Guest management, table layout, seating moves, constraint rules, and a solver. Any agent that speaks WebMCP can drive this board.
Watch the agent call auto underscore seat. Twenty-four guests seated instantly — every rule honored, families and friend groups kept together, and the locked seats untouched. Zero violations.
Now the human half. The host drags Uncle Jim right next to Aunt Carol. The violations panel catches the divorce rule immediately — the board itself knows the social rules.

One tool call later, the agent has repaired the room around the host's other choices. And when the agent tries to move a locked guest — it's refused. The human always wins. Every agent action streams into the activity feed, so trust runs both directions.
New drama arrives mid-planning: Priya and Dev, ex-coworkers, awkward. The agent records the rule with a note, re-solves, and the board is clean again.
No backend, no build step — just a static page whose tools any WebMCP agent can call, with a human's hands on the same board. SeatCraft: humans drag, agents solve.
